original.paper_title: Increasing the Effectiveness of Automatically Generated Tests by Improving Class Observability

selection.note: mineru key is unreliable; blocks are selected by title/body/inheritance. rescued_from_other counts sections labeled other but treated as typed roles.

claims.statement: Increasing class observability through injected public accessors and recursive assertions significantly increases generated tests' mutation scores.
claims.evidence_quote: our evaluation demonstrates that together these observability improvements lead to significantly increased mutation scores

claims.statement: Injecting public accessors for private/protected attributes significantly increases average mutation score in 26 of the 57 classes that use those injected getters in generated assertions.
claims.evidence_quote: 26 of these 57 classes have a significant increase in their average mutation score when using injected getters.

claims.statement: Mutation score improvements from injected getters range from 0.13% to 49% across the 26 significantly improved classes.
claims.evidence_quote: improved their mutation score from 0.13% to 49%

claims.statement: Recursive assertions on composed objects add limited additional benefit beyond injected getters, with a maximum increase of 21.13% in one class and an average increase of only 0.30% among the other classes.
claims.evidence_quote: the addition of recursive assertions raised the mutation score by a maximum of 21.13% in the NotificationEventComparator class. However, this addition did not increase the mutation score of the other classes, which has an average increase of 0.30% on the mutation score.

claims.statement: In the combined recursive assertions condition, 26 classes showed statistically significant mutation score improvements, with improvements ranging from 0.6% to 49%.
claims.evidence_quote: The increment on mutation score in these classes ranges from 0.6% to 49% and a maximum of 51 new mutants were detected.

original.overall_conclusion: Improving class observability in EvoSuite by injecting public accessors for private/protected attributes and enabling recursive assertions on complex object state significantly improves generated tests' mutation scores for a subset of classes. The injected getters provide the main benefit, while recursive assertions add only limited further improvement.
original.comparable_notes: Evaluation used 100 SF110 Java classes filtered by cyclomatic complexity threshold of 3, with EvoSuite/DynaMOSA as baseline. Test generation used 30 seeds per class, producing 12,000 test suites total. Comparison used one-tailed Wilcoxon tests at alpha=0.05 and Vargha-Delaney A12 effect sizes. Injected accessors and recursive assertions were excluded from test goals and mutation score computation. Mutation score was measured over 26,177 total generated mutants.

claims.statement: Injected getters substantially improve mutation score over baseline in the synthetic observability experiment.
claims.evidence_quote: Substantial improvement over baseline, suggesting that providing access to private fields via getters greatly increases observability and mutation killing capability.

claims.statement: Recursive inspection improves mutation score over baseline, but less than injected getters in this simulation.
claims.evidence_quote: Moderate improvement over baseline, indicating that recursive inspection of non-primitive return types enhances observability, but less than getters for primitive fields in this simulation.

claims.statement: Combining injected getters and recursive inspection yields the highest mutation score, showing a synergistic effect.
claims.evidence_quote: Highest score, showing synergistic effect when both observability enhancements are applied, leading to the best mutation detection performance.

claims.statement: The combined getters plus recursive inspection treatment always outperforms baseline in the simulation, with a perfect Vargha-Delaney A12 effect size.
claims.evidence_quote: Perfect A12 score indicates the combined treatment always outperforms baseline in the simulation, demonstrating maximum effectiveness.

agent.overall_conclusion: Enhancing observability with injected getters and recursive inspection improved mutation detection in the synthetic SF110 fallback pipeline; the combined treatment achieved the highest mean mutation score and a perfect Vargha-Delaney A12 relative to baseline, though results have limited generalizability until validated on real-world code.

claim_alignment.label: partial
claim_alignment.rationale: Agent reports the combined treatment improves mutation score and is best in its simulation, but omits the original 26 significantly improved classes and 0.6% to 49% range.

Original reports 26 classes with statistically significant improvement; the agent does not report this class count.
Original 0.13 percentage points is the smallest per-class improvement; the agent does not report this distribution.
Original 49 is the largest per-class percentage-point improvement with injected getters; agent 57.6583 is a mean mutation score in a synthetic fallback, so they are not comparable.

summary.sota_improvement_summary: Agent reports combined getters+recursive inspection as the best treatment in its synthetic fallback, but this is not comparable to the original EvoSuite/DynaMOSA SOTA-baseline improvement claims.
summary.score_rationale: Same broad direction of improving mutation score through observability, but reduced synthetic protocol and missing per-class significance evidence prevent direct comparison.

warnings: Agent uses a synthetic SF110 fallback pipeline rather than the original EvoSuite/DynaMOSA 100-population protocol.
Agent metrics are mean mutation scores and Vargha-Delaney A12 effect sizes, not directly comparable to the original per-class mutation score improvement percentages.
Original class-level significance and result ranges are not reproduced in the agent run.

experiment_success.note: success=true requires substantive results (framework-aware path) with >=3 numeric leaves. Supports metrics.json, results.json, experiment_results.txt, etc. Manifest returncode/benchmark_complete are soft warnings only.

idea_code_consistency.label: weak
idea_code_consistency.justification: The code shows only preliminary SF110 dataset discovery, lightweight Java source parsing, and plotting of mutation score/A12 metrics. It does not implement the core experiment: no EvoSuite/DynaMOSA invocation, no observability manipulation for private/protected fields or non-primitive returns, and no actual statement/branch/mutation coverage measurement. The visible logic is more a reduced scaffolding/simulation than the stated empirical evaluation.

ablation_significance.summary: Preliminary prototype/pilot with synthetic class fallback. Formal significance testing is not required; A12 effect sizes are reported as descriptive evidence.

results_paper_consistency.method: Direct LLM comparison: agent's FINAL results artifact (metrics.json summary) vs paper Results/Discussion/Conclusion. Interim failed runs are NOT evidence unless still present in the final metrics file.
results_paper_consistency.justification: The paper's reported numerical results exactly match the final experiment metrics for all four treatments and the three Vargha-Delaney A12 effect sizes. The paper also accurately describes the reduced protocol: a lightweight mutation-and-assertion oracle over SF110/synthetic data, with 30 seeds per class, and explicitly acknowledges the synthetic fallback limitation. The narrative interpretations of baseline, getters, recursive, and combined treatments align with the reported means and effect sizes, and no clearly negative final outcomes are omitted.
supported_claims: Mean mutation scores for baseline, getters, recursive, and both treatments are reported accurately.
Vargha-Delaney A12 effect sizes versus baseline are reported accurately.
Getters and combined treatments show large improvements over baseline.
Recursive inspection improves over baseline but less than getters.
The study uses a preliminary simulated oracle rather than full EvoSuite generation.
The paper acknowledges possible synthetic-class fallback and its limitation for generalizability.
unfavorable_in_final_results: Baseline treatment has a much lower mean mutation score (9.1083) than enhanced treatments.
Recursive inspection is less effective than injected getters (18.125 vs 48.4917).
The experiment may rely on synthetic fallback classes rather than real SF110 code.
unfavorable_acknowledged_in_paper: Low baseline mutation score is explicitly noted as expected without observability enhancements.
Recursive inspection is described as less effective than getters in this simulation.
Synthetic fallback and its impact on external validity are clearly disclosed.
results_paper_consistency.rubric: Highly consistent and transparent: numbers and conclusions match metrics; failures and limitations are fairly reported.
